We arrived at 1:40 PM in Cabos San Lucas and traveled to Centro de Investigaciones Biológicas del Noroeste among other locations. Dr. Whitmore was studying Brown thrashers and Yellow "Mangrove" warblers, in particular. This was a memorable trip and contributed toward my curiosity and admiration of desert ecosystems, rural lifestyles, and global surf culture. The people were kind and interesting. I spent the last 1.5 hours of light seawatching, though we unfortunately only had 2 working scopes on hand. As has been the case this year, seawatching was excellent here, though a more prolonged visit with good lighting would've been preferable (alas, the others were not as hot on a return visit!). The Storm-Petrel showing, so impressive 2 weeks prior, had completely dissipated, but was replaced by large numbers of fulmars and other seabirds. ----Day notes: Our first day in the Vizcaino was definitely the best, surely in part due to hitting many good spots for the first time in weeks allowing birds to pile up. We started at asuncion and hit a series of locations westbound along the highway ending finally over at Punta Eugenia with a fun dusk seawatch in the wind.
